summary: Suzanne Siauve worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at École Normale Supérieure de Sèvres, under Louis Renou and Jacques Bacot, and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Paris, later serving at CNRS and Institut de France.

Sven Hedin was an Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Stockholm University, Uppsala University (M.A.), Humboldt University of Berlin under Ferdinand von Richthofen, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (Ph.D.).

Sven S. Hartman specialized in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, Stig Wikander, and Geo Widengren, later holding posts at Uppsala, Åbo Akademi University, and Lund University.
Sven Sellmer is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He has held academic posts at the University of Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Svetozar Petrović worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Zagreb and University of Allahabad, later serving in literature posts at the University of Zagreb, University of Novi Sad, and University of Belgrade.

Swami Japasiddhananda specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Karnataka State Open University, and Visva-Bharati University, later working at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya and Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute.

Swami Lakshman Joo was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies figure who studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan and founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991. He taught scholars including Lilian Silburn, André Padoux, and Alexis Sanderson.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj focused on philosophy and Indology. He served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha (attested 1980) and founded both the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied and held a post at the University of Calcutta, and taught Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara.

Swami Shivananda was a religious studies, philosophy, and Indology figure who studied at Thanjavur Medical College. He taught Mircea Eliade and Swami Vishnudevananda, and founded the Divine Life Society and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.
Swami Siddheswarananda worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras from ~1913 to ~1917 and served in the Ramakrishna Order from ~1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda was active in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda was an Indology and religious studies figure. He studied under Swami Shivananda as a disciple from ~1947 to ~1963 and founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda was a religious studies, philosophy, and Indology figure. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and University of Calcutta, was a disciple of Ramakrishna, and taught William Hastie, Margaret Elizabeth Noble, and others.

Swayam Bagaria works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Grinnell College and Johns Hopkins University (Doctorate), later holding posts as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Virginia and assistant professor at Harvard University.

Sweta Prajapati is an Indology scholar who earned her Ph.D. at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. She served as Director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and Director in-Charge at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Sybrandus Johannes Warren was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his studies and Ph.D. under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University, later serving as Director of Johan de Witt-gymnasium and Erasmiaans Gymnasium.
Sydney Frank Markham was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Wadham College (~1920–1923) and served as Secretary and then President of the Museums Association (~1929–1942).

Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Patna College, Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, Royal School of Mines, and University of London, later serving the Government of Hyderabad and as Reader at the University of Cambridge.
